name: Benchmarks and Agent Testing
gist: Papers that create tests and benchmarks to measure how well agents can use tools and accomplish goals.
explain: Before you can improve something, you have to measure it, because without numbers you don't know if a change actually helped or if it just feels faster. This subtheme covers the tests and benchmarks researchers create to evaluate how well agents use tools. A benchmark is a standard problem set with known right answers: here are 1,000 questions, agents try to answer them by using available tools, and we score how many they got right, which lets researchers compare different agent designs fairly and track progress over time instead of just guessing. Some benchmarks test specific skills like whether agents can correctly chain tools together, and others are more open-ended, like 'solve this real-world research question'.

The challenge in building good benchmarks is that tool use is contextual and hard to judge automatically. Did the agent succeed because it is actually smart at planning, or because it got lucky and guessed right? If an agent takes a different but correct path to the answer, how do you score that? Some tools might be optional (you could use them but don't have to), and the benchmark has to figure out whether skipping them is smart or lazy. And there is constant pressure for benchmarks to become easier: agents and researchers figure out shortcuts, and the benchmark stops being a real test of capability.

Papers in this area create benchmarks that test specific aspects of tool use: can agents plan multi-step solutions? Can they recover from tool failures? Can they use tools they have never seen before? Some benchmarks are focused on real-world scenarios like writing code or querying databases, while others are more abstract. The best benchmarks are challenging enough that agents today only solve them some of the time, which means the benchmark still has life in it and motivates research to get better.

papers.title: Agent Data Protocol
papers.contribution: Unified 13 existing agent datasets via ADP, achieved ~20% average performance gain over base models, and state-of-the-art or near-SOTA on coding, browsing, tool use, and research benchmarks.

papers.title: AgentHijack: Benchmarking Computer Use Agent Robustness to Common Environment Corruptions
papers.contribution: Reveals fragility of current agents to minor corruptions and demonstrates effectiveness of robustness-aware approach.

papers.title: ComplexMCP: Evaluation of LLM Agents in Dynamic, Interdependent, and Large-Scale Tool Sandbox
papers.contribution: Reveals stark performance gap with top models failing to exceed 60% success rate versus human 90%, identifying three fundamental bottlenecks: tool retrieval saturation, over-confidence, and strategic defeatism.

papers.title: DRBench: A Realistic Benchmark for Enterprise Deep Research
papers.contribution: Evaluation of diverse agents on DRBench demonstrates their strengths and weaknesses, highlighting critical paths for advancing enterprise deep research.

papers.title: Holistic Agent Leaderboard: The Missing Infrastructure for AI Agent Evaluation
papers.contribution: Conducts 21,730 agent rollouts across 9 models and 9 benchmarks, reducing evaluation time from weeks to hours, revealing surprising insights and previously unreported behaviors.

papers.title: Investigating Component Contributions in Multi-Agent ML Systems
papers.contribution: Finds iterative feedback contributes more than architectural complexity and multi-agent coordination can hurt as often as help, providing concrete guidance for practitioners.

papers.title: SciAgentGym: Benchmarking Multi-Step Scientific Tool-Use in LLM Agents
papers.contribution: Demonstrates that fine-tuned SciAgent-8B outperforms Qwen3-VL-235B-Instruct with positive cross-domain transfer of scientific tool-use capabilities.

papers.title: SciNet: Evaluating AI Agents in Relation-Aware Scientific Literature Retrieval
papers.contribution: Shows current retrieval agents achieve below 20% accuracy on relation-aware tasks, while agents with SciNet achieve 25.3% improvement in downstream review quality.

papers.title: $\tau$-Voice: Benchmarking Full-Duplex Voice Agents on Real-World Domains
papers.contribution: Voice agents retain only 30-45% of text performance under realistic conditions; 79-90% of failures stem from agent behavior; provides reproducible testbed.

papers.title: A Computational Framework for Evaluating Human-likeness in LLMs' Open-ended Human Behaviors
papers.contribution: Reveals that even the best current LLMs exhibit significant gap from real user behavior in online shopping, Q&A, and urban mobility, underscoring need for human-like capability research.

papers.title: AOEB: Benchmarking Agent-Oriented Multimodal Embeddings
papers.contribution: Reveals that embedding models exhibit distinct strengths across different agent-oriented tasks, promoting practically oriented direction within embedding community.

papers.title: AOrchestra: Automating Sub-Agent Creation for Agentic Orchestration
papers.contribution: Achieves 16.28% relative improvement over strongest baseline on challenging benchmarks while reducing human engineering effort.

papers.title: AgentNoiseBench: Benchmarking Robustness of Tool-Using LLM Agents Under Noisy Condition
papers.contribution: Reveals consistent performance variations and sensitivity of current agentic models to realistic environmental perturbations through systematic evaluation.

papers.title: AgentSelect: Benchmark for Narrative Query-to-Agent Recommendation
papers.contribution: The benchmark reveals a shift from dense head reuse to long-tail supervision and demonstrates that content-aware intent-to-capability matching outperforms ID-based methods.

papers.title: AppWorld-UL: Benchmarking Diverse Agent-User Interactions for Tool-Use
papers.contribution: Evaluation reveals Claude Opus 4.7 achieves only 48.6% success on AppWorld-UL and 21.3% on compositional tasks at scenario-level, demonstrating the benchmark's difficulty.

papers.title: Benchmarking Agent Memory in Interdependent Multi-Session Agentic Tasks
papers.contribution: Reveals agents with near-saturated performance on existing long-context benchmarks perform poorly in agentic setting, exposing gap in current evaluations.

papers.title: BioAgent Bench: An AI Agent Evaluation Suite for Bioinformatics
papers.contribution: Shows frontier LLMs can complete pipelines reliably but fail under perturbations; identifies need for local agents to preserve patient data privacy.

papers.title: CoopEval: Benchmarking Cooperation-Sustaining Mechanisms and LLM Agents in Social Dilemmas
papers.contribution: Demonstrates that contracting and mediation are most effective for capable LLM cooperation, and that evolutionary pressures improve mechanism effectiveness.

papers.title: DIVE: Scaling Diversity in Agentic Task Synthesis for Generalizable Tool Use
papers.contribution: Training on 48k DIVE trajectories over 374 tools improves Qwen3-8B by +22 points on 9 OOD benchmarks, outperforming strongest 8B baseline by +68%.

papers.title: DSGym: A Standardized and Holistic Framework for Evaluating and Training Data Science Agents
papers.contribution: Enables end-to-end measurement of agent planning, implementation, and validation; training on 2,000 examples substantially improves 4B model on benchmarks.

papers.title: DynaSchedBench: Calibrated Dynamic Scheduling Benchmarks and Observability Paradox in LLM-based Scheduling Agents
papers.contribution: Identifies key limitations of LLM-based scheduling agents, including an Observability Paradox where oracle information can degrade policy performance.

papers.title: EVMbench: Evaluating AI Agents on Smart Contract Security
papers.contribution: Frontier agents can discover and exploit vulnerabilities end-to-end against live blockchain instances, advancing understanding of agent security capabilities.

papers.title: Earth-Agent: Unlocking the Full Landscape of Earth Observation with Agents
papers.contribution: Enables complex scientific tasks like geophysical parameter retrieval and quantitative spatiotemporal analysis beyond pretrained MLLMs; establishes new paradigm for scientifically grounded EO analysis.

papers.title: EnterpriseOps-Gym: Environments and Evaluations for Stateful Agentic Planning and Tool Use in Enterprise Settings
papers.contribution: Reveals critical limitations: top model (Claude Sonnet 4.5) achieves only 34.1% success, exposing unreadiness for enterprise deployment.

papers.title: FIRE-Bench: Evaluating AI Agents on the Rediscovery of Scientific Insights
papers.contribution: Shows even strongest agents achieve limited rediscovery success below 50 F1 with high variance and recurring failures in experimental design and evidence-based reasoning.

papers.title: From Reproduction to Replication: Evaluating Research Agents with Progressive Code Masking
papers.contribution: Performance degrades rapidly as difficulty increases; interactive debugging agents outperform fixed harnesses.

papers.title: FullStack-Agent: Enhancing Agentic Full-Stack Web Coding via Development-Oriented Testing and Repository Back-Translation
papers.contribution: Outperforms previous state-of-the-art by 8.7% on frontend, 38.2% on backend, and 15.9% on database tests; self-improvement raises 30B model performance by 9.7-9.5% across test cases.

papers.title: Functional Cache Grafting: Robust and Rapid Code-Policy Synthesis for Embodied Agents
papers.contribution: The approach achieves 18.31% higher task success rate and 2.3× faster policy synthesis than prompt-level caching methods.

papers.title: GameDevBench: Evaluating Agentic Capabilities Through Game Development
papers.contribution: Present the first game development benchmark for agents; show best methods solve only 53.8% of tasks and that visual feedback increases GPT-4's performance from 41.1% to 52.0%.

papers.title: Hunt Instead of Wait: Evaluating Deep Data Research on Large Language Models
papers.contribution: Evaluates mainstream VLA models and frontier LLMs, revealing that effective investigatory intelligence requires intrinsic agentic strategies beyond scaffolding or scaling.

papers.title: KernelCraft: Benchmarking for Agentic Close-to-Metal Kernel Generation on Emerging Hardware
papers.contribution: Demonstrates leading reasoning models generate functionally correct kernels for unseen ISAs within refinement steps and produce optimized kernels matching compiler baselines.

papers.title: Large-Scale Terminal Agentic Trajectory Generation from Dockerized Environments
papers.contribution: Models trained on TerminalTraj data achieve consistent improvements on TerminalBench with gains up to 20% on TB 1.0 and 10% on TB 2.0; TerminalTraj-32B reaches 35.30% on TB 1.0 and 22.00% on TB 2.0 with improved scaling.

papers.title: MCP-Persona: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Real-World Personal Applications via Environment Simulation
papers.contribution: The benchmark reveals significant struggles of current agents with personalized tool use and is released publicly, highlighting the need for better agent evaluation on practical applications.

papers.title: NL2Repo-Bench: Towards Long-Horizon Repository Generation Evaluation of Coding Agents
papers.contribution: Experiments show that long-horizon repository generation remains largely unsolved with frontier agents achieving merely 40% average test pass rates, identifying systematic failure modes including premature termination, loss of global coherence, and fragile cro

papers.title: PerfGuard: A Performance-Aware Agent for Visual Content Generation
papers.contribution: PerfGuard improves tool selection accuracy, execution reliability, and alignment with user intent for complex AIGC tasks compared to state-of-the-art methods.

papers.title: Persona2Web: Benchmarking Personalized Web Agents for Contextual Reasoning with User History
papers.contribution: First benchmark for evaluating personalized web agents on open web, revealing key challenges across agent architectures, models, history schemes, and ambiguity levels.

papers.title: ProAct: A Benchmark and Multimodal Framework for Structure-Aware Proactive Response
papers.contribution: ProAct-Helper improves trigger detection mF1 by 6.21%, reduces steps by 0.25, and increases parallel action rate by 15.58% compared to strong closed-source baselines.

papers.title: Programming with Pixels: Can Computer-Use Agents do Software Engineering?
papers.contribution: When given access to file editing and bash APIs, generalist CUAs reach levels comparable to specialized coding agents; visual-only performance is significantly worse.

papers.title: ROGA: Scaling Generalist Agents for Office Productivity Tasks via Tool Generation
papers.contribution: ROGA addresses fundamental paradigm limitations, showing current ATG agents underperform by up to 27.43%, and demonstrates ROGA's effectiveness on long-horizon office productivity benchmarks.

papers.title: Routing and Reasoned Evaluation with Large Language Models
papers.contribution: Provides systematic analysis of how reasoning traces correlate with assessment outcomes; develops offline and online routing strategies achieving substantially improved accuracy-efficiency trade-offs across 19 language models.

papers.title: SWE-Perf: Can Language Models Optimize Code Performance on Real-World Repositories?
papers.contribution: Comprehensive evaluation of representative LLM methods reveals a substantial capability gap between existing models and expert-level optimization performance.

papers.title: ScaleCUA: Scaling Open-Source Computer Use Agents with Cross-Platform Data
papers.contribution: Sets new state-of-the-art results with 94.4% on MMBench-GUI L1-Hard, 60.6% on OSWorld-G, and 47.4% on WebArena-Lite-v2, demonstrating data-driven scaling for computer use agents.

papers.title: Shoot First, Ask Questions Later? Building Rational Agents that Explore and Act Like People
papers.contribution: Monte Carlo BED-based methods boost Spotter accuracy by up to 14.7% and raise expected information gain by up to 0.227 bits; combined with Captain strategy yields up to 0.374 F1 improvement and enables weaker models to outperform frontier models.

papers.title: The Tool Decathlon: Benchmarking Language Agents for Diverse, Realistic, and Long-Horizon Task Execution
papers.contribution: Largest and most diverse benchmark for language agents with reliable execution-based evaluation across real-world applications.

papers.title: Tools are under-documented: Simple Document Expansion Boosts Tool Retrieval
papers.contribution: Document expansion substantially improves retrieval performance, achieving state-of-the-art on both ToolRet and Tool-DE benchmarks with 50k and 200k instances respectively.

papers.title: VeRO: A Harness for Agents to Optimize Agents
papers.contribution: VeRO empirically studies which code modifications reliably improve target agent harnesses and supports research on agent optimization.

papers.title: VenusBench-Mobile: A Challenging and User-Centric Benchmark for Mobile GUI Agents with Capability Diagnostics
papers.contribution: Reveals large performance gaps relative to prior benchmarks, shows failures dominated by perception and memory deficiencies, and demonstrates agents exhibit near-zero success under environment variations.

papers.title: What Do Agents Learn from Trajectory-SFT: Semantics or Interfaces?
papers.contribution: Reveals that trajectory-SFT can amplify interface reliance, showing agents degrade sharply under minimal interface rewrites, with interface shortcutting exhibiting environment-dependent non-monotonic training dynamics invisible to standard evaluation.

papers.title: ZeroGR: A Generalizable and Scalable Framework for Zero-Shot Generative Retrieval
papers.contribution: ZeroGR outperforms dense retrieval and generative baselines on BEIR and MAIR zero-shot benchmarks, establishing state-of-the-art for instruction-driven generative retrieval.
